hints: Consider the forces acting on the trailer alone: the forward tension $T$ from the tow-bar and the backward resistance of $100\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the trailer of mass $400\text{ kg}$ accelerating forward at $1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$: $T - 100 = 400(1.5)$.
Solve for $T$ by adding $100$ to the calculated product.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law in the direction of motion to the trailer of mass $400\text{ kg}$ with forward acceleration $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and resistance $100\text{ N}$:
$$T - 100 = 400(1.5)$$

Solve for the tension $T$ in the tow-bar:
$$T - 100 = 600$$
$$T = 600 + 100 = 700\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Isolate the trailer as a single particle. Identify all horizontal forces acting on it: the tension $T$ pulling forward and the resistance force $R_{\text{trailer}} = 100\text{ N}$ opposing motion.

State Newton's second law in the direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = ma$$
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} = m_{\text{trailer}}a$$

Substitute the known values $m_{\text{trailer}} = 400\text{ kg}$, $R_{\text{trailer}} = 100\text{ N}$, and $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T - 100 = 400(1.5)$$

Compute the product on the right-hand side and solve for $T$:
$$400 \times 1.5 = 600$$
$$T - 100 = 600$$
Add $100$ to both sides:
$$T = 600 + 100 = 700\text{ N}$$

hints: Find the driving force $F_D$ by applying Newton's second law to the whole system of combined mass $1800 + 400 = 2200\text{ kg}$.
Form the equation of motion: $F_D - 250 - 100 = 2200(1.5)$ and solve for $F_D$.
Calculate the engine power at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $P = F_D v$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the car and trailer as a combined system of total mass $1800 + 400 = 2200\text{ kg}$ with acceleration $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$F_D - 250 - 100 = 2200(1.5)$$

Calculate the driving force $F_D$ of the car's engine:
$$F_D - 350 = 3300$$
$$F_D = 3300 + 350 = 3650\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power of the engine at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $P = F_D v$:
$$P = F_D v = 3650 \times 20 = 73000\text{ W} = 73\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Consider the whole connected system of car and trailer. The internal tow-bar tension cancels out, leaving the driving force $F_D$ and total resistance opposing motion.

State Newton's second law for the combined system:
$$\sum F = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$F_D - R_{\text{car}} - R_{\text{trailer}} = (m_{\text{car}} + m_{\text{trailer}})a$$

State the relationship between power, driving force, and velocity:
$$P = F_D \times v$$
Substitute the driving force $F_D = 3650\text{ N}$ and instantaneous speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 3650 \times 20 = 73000\text{ W}$$
Dividing by $1000$ yields $73\text{ kW}$.
